notes.note: #2932 part 2 round 3: session-api.md corrected its chained-command passage under respondToRequest (every PowerShell ask prompts; the three things a Bash grant answers inside a chain). The ADR cites the session API only as the current orchestration surface; its decisions do not concern approval grants.

#2932 part 2 round 3: corrected the page after live probes against the bundled 2.1.278 CLI disproved two round-2 statements. Removed the claim that matched_ask_rule is set for a prefix ask rule on a part (a chain with Bash(git push:*) on one part and another part needing approval arrives with no matched_ask_rule), and the claim that a PowerShell grant answers an ordinary PowerShell ask. Now states: subcommandResults on PowerShell always escalates because a single command's security warning is wrapped exactly like an ordinary command; subcommandResults on Bash is a plain call by owner decision unless classifier_approvable, reason text, a matched ask rule or an earlier signal is present; a decision_reason_code escalates. Rewrote the gap list as (i) any ask rule on one part, exact or prefix, when another part also needs approval, (ii) a write or delete outside the working directories in an && or ; chain or in a pipeline with an output redirect, (iii) a part's non-safety warning, with the two guarantees (a safety check on any part, an ask rule on a single command) and the statement that the gaps exist on main and need the engine to send nested reasons. Checked every listed shape against the nine captured request bodies now committed as fixtures/claude-2.1.278-chained-bash-asks.json and the adapter test that replays each under a Bash grant (five answered, four prompting), and against claudeAskEscalates and its shared cases. The tee pipeline keeping addDirectories and the ls-plus-ruled-part case arriving as type rule are both in the captures.
